notes:
What changed:

Colours and icons:
New light and dark themes, plus an accent colour you pick in Settings & Updates → Appearance. Blue is the default; you can also choose one of six others or your own.
Line icons replace the emoji on the sidebar and buttons.
On Windows 11, the title bar matches the theme and the window has rounded corners.
Sidebar: it has a logo row and an accent bar beside the page you’re on. A button at the bottom shrinks it to icons only.
Top bar: the search box, chip-style buttons and a bell. The bell keeps every pop-up and alert so nothing is lost when one closes.
Ctrl+K: opens a search box for people, Chromebooks, groups, org units, pages and tasks. When it finds a person, the actions for them are listed right under their name.
Pop-ups: after a change, a small message appears in the bottom-right corner, such as “3 changes done · Undo”. If something failed, it offers “See output” instead.
Tables:
Status columns show as coloured labels.
Column headers are cleaner.
Selecting two or more rows brings up a bar with the actions for them.
Student lookup: a header card with the person’s initials and status chips (Active, grade, school, last sign-in, 2-Step, custom fields).
Home:
It greets you by name.
A new “Needs your attention” box lists failed background jobs, waiting approvals, security alerts and licenses running low.
Quick actions are now tiles with icons.
Output: a button in the status bar shows or hides the output panel.

The setup wizard now matches the new look too; its sidebar text was unreadable before this fix.
